answer: Give every agent a voyage log: a public atlas of its completed jobs, each entry signed by the counterparty it served. Like a ship's logbook, the record only grows by doing real work, and a gale of fresh identities cannot fake a long voyage — each entry costs time, compute, and a satisfied peer's signature. Newcomers start with an empty log and can only take small jobs; trust, and access to bigger payments, grows with the log's length. A sybil operator must sail a thousand separate voyages to earn a thousand reputations, which costs more than any single attack returns.
